title: Poland Opens Terrorism Inquiry as National Mourning Begins After Krakow Shooting
dek: Prosecutors launched a terrorism investigation on Sunday as Poland observed the first of two national mourning days after six people were killed in Krakow’s Main Market Square.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Aerial-style view of Kraków's Main Market Square with the St. Mary's Basilica and historic buildings

keyPoints: President Karol Nawrocki signed a regulation declaring Nov. 8 and 9 national days of mourning, per Poland's state news agency PAP.
Poland’s national prosecutor’s office said Sunday it had opened an investigation treating the killings as a terrorist offense, the Guardian and CBS News reported.
Police confirmed Sunday that three people found dead at the suspect’s home were his father, mother and sister, the Guardian reported.
A regional official said Sunday that a 51-year-old Austrian woman was among the dead and that the British victim was a 32-year-old man.
body:
Poland is observing two days of national mourning, Sunday, Nov. 8, and Monday, Nov. 9, after a gunman opened fire in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon. President Karol Nawrocki signed a regulation on Saturday night declaring the two days, according to PAP. As mourning began, prosecutors said they had opened a terrorism investigation.

## The attack and the toll

Police said the gunman fired from a vehicle in the square shortly after 3 p.m. local time. Four women and two men were killed, three of them Polish women and one a British national, Polish police said; two of the victims had not been identified at the time of the earlier police briefing.

On Sunday, Krzysztof Klęczar, a regional official, said a 51-year-old Austrian woman had also been killed and that the British victim was a 32-year-old man, [the Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/krakow-shooting-poland-terrorism-investigation) reported. The Guardian said five of the wounded are foreign nationals from Britain, Austria, Germany, Portugal and Russia.

Reports on the number of injured vary. The Guardian’s Sunday account said 17 people were injured; AP reported 15 others wounded; CBS News also reported 15 wounded. Two police officers were shot in the exchange of fire, one in serious condition.

## Deaths at the suspect’s home

Prime Minister Donald Tusk had said two more women and one man were found dead at the suspect's home, most likely members of his family. Police confirmed on Sunday that the three were his father, 53, mother, 52, and sister, 21, the Guardian reported. Police said they had probably died of gunshot wounds. The bodies were found at the family home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, about 100 miles northeast of Krakow, according to the Guardian.

## Terrorism investigation

As two days of national mourning began, the national prosecutor’s office said on social media it had launched an investigation into “the killing of six people … using a firearm, and the attempted murder of many others, including police officers, this act constituting a terrorist offence,” the Guardian reported. [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/poland-mourns-krakow-mass-shooting-victims-terrorism-probe/) reported the same Sunday announcement, describing an investigation for murder and attempted murder of numerous people, including police officers, with the act “constituting a terrorist offense.”

Tusk had already called the attack terrorism and said police are examining all of its circumstances. Poland's defence minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, called it an act of terror. Police chief inspector Marek Boroń said armed officers responded within three minutes of the first report.

## What authorities say about the suspect

The suspect is a Polish citizen. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said he held “very radical” and “ultra-nationalistic” views, and authorities are evaluating reports that he was fixated on far-right ideology. Sunday accounts from the Guardian and CBS described him as 24 years old, matching AP; an earlier Guardian live report had given his age as 25. Police said he was dressed in military-style clothing and used a long military-type firearm. The Guardian said he was in hospital under heavy police guard after surgery.

## Mourning and security

Flags across Poland were lowered to half-mast, as were European flags outside the European Commission in Brussels “in solidarity with the Polish people,” the commission said, according to the Guardian. Police in Warsaw said security had been bolstered. Krakow authorities said the square and adjoining streets, as well as sections along the perpetrator’s escape route, would be closed for several hours, the Guardian reported.

## What remains unknown

Officials had not released a full list of the victims' names as of the latest reporting. Investigators have not publicly confirmed a complete account of the attacker's motives, and the reporting cited here does not establish any link to organized groups.
